topics.title: US-Iran hostilities shake Gulf region
topics.summary: Fresh U.S. strikes on Iran and Iranian retaliation against Gulf targets raised diplomatic alarm, tightened oil-route worries, and prompted calls for restraint from several countries.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a tense situation suddenly affected everyone nearby, who in the studio would push for a calm group plan first?

topics.title: Markets steady after oil jump
topics.summary: U.S. stocks rose as oil prices and bond yields held steadier after recent pressure, while investors watched energy costs, inflation signals, and upcoming jobs data.
topics.discussionPrompt: When prices get jumpy, what would the studio protect first: snacks, props, coffee, or comfy chairs?

topics.title: Xi visits Egypt in Mideast push
topics.summary: China's Xi Jinping visited Egypt to deepen economic and diplomatic ties, with Suez Canal access and wider Middle East influence high on the agenda.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio wanted a bigger role in the neighborhood, would it start with favors, parties, or serious meetings?

topics.title: UN warns climate goal will overshoot
topics.summary: A UN report says global heating is likely to pass the 1.5C target before any later cooling path, adding urgency to emissions cuts and adaptation plans.
topics.discussionPrompt: What everyday change would the studio actually stick with if everyone had to lower waste without making life miserable?

topics.title: Ukraine warns on Russian airspace
topics.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned airlines that Russian airspace is increasingly unsafe because of drone activity, as attacks on rail, energy, and port infrastructure continued.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a normal route suddenly felt risky, who would find a clever detour and who would overpack for the trip?

topics.title: Data centre backlash grows
topics.summary: Communities are pushing back against rapid data centre expansion, arguing AI-driven projects can strain energy, water, planning rules, and local trust.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio needed a giant computer room, what would neighbors fairly want to know before saying yes?

topics.title: Nvidia urges practical AI rules
topics.summary: At a G20 technology meeting, Nvidia's Jensen Huang urged governments to regulate real-world AI problems instead of hypothetical harms, joining a wider industry push.
topics.discussionPrompt: When making rules for a powerful new tool, should the studio ban weird possibilities or wait for real problems?

topics.title: UK AI strategist joins Anthropic
topics.summary: Matt Clifford, who helped shape Britain's AI strategy, joined Anthropic in an international affairs role, drawing scrutiny over tech policy influence and conflicts.
topics.discussionPrompt: If someone helped write the studio rules, how long should they wait before working for a company affected by them?

topics.title: US grid faces heatwave strain
topics.summary: U.S. energy officials warned that heatwave demand could raise blackout risks across major electric grids, especially in the PJM region serving 67 million people.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the power got unreliable at the studio, what low-tech backup plan would everyone secretly enjoy?

topics.title: Pesticide study highlights farmer risks
topics.summary: A new analysis says pesticide poisoning affects a large share of the world's farmers each year, renewing debate over safety rules, training, and alternatives.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a job needs risky materials, what would make the workplace feel responsible instead of just saying be careful?
